column2: Work back from the selling price: target cost = selling price − required profit.
Break the product target down to subsystems, then parts, by function, by share of the previous product’s cost, or a mix of both.
Estimate what the present or concept design costs, using analogous data or a bottom-up cost model, to get the gap to target.
Identify which features, materials, tolerances and processes drive the gap, and where a small design change moves cost most.
Generate options such as fewer parts, simpler geometry, standard materials, relaxed tolerances or a different process, and re-estimate each against performance, quality and safety requirements.
Report cost against target at every design review, and treat an overrun like a missed weight or performance requirement, with an action, an owner and a date.
